accelerator_ids.description: bare record ids of the accelerators obtainable here

channels.description: sales motion: direct-quote | reseller | marketplace | auction | rental | on-prem-cloud | contact-sales

price_usd.description: unit or configured-system price; unit basis in notes

price_basis.description: what the price covers: bare card, SXM module, full 8-GPU server, annual rental, per-hour cloud, incl. tax/shipping, etc.

lead_time_source.description: provenance of lead_time_weeks, which is otherwise unreadable when null. published = the vendor or channel states it. midpoint-inference = inferred from two published points. structural-na = the number does not apply because the channel is structurally instant (on-demand cloud rental, peer-to-peer marketplace, spot capacity) — NOT the same as 'nobody publishes it'. unknown = not established.

lead_time_basis.description: why lead_time_weeks has the value it has, or why it is null: the measurement window, whether it is a quote-date range, and for structural-na the reason no number applies.

export_controlled.description: true if sale is restricted by region/entity. The BOOLEAN ALONE is not enough to act on: name the regime in export_control_regime and the mechanism in export_control_note.

export_control_regime.description: the actual citation, e.g. 'EAR 3A090.a', 'EAR 3A090.a.1 / 3E001', 'EAR 744.23 (Entity List)', 'EAR 126.18 (military end use)'. Free text on purpose: these are not a closed set, and a wrong enum value here is a compliance error, not a typo. Cite the paragraph, not a country list.

export_control_note.description: the mechanism: which licence or exception, whether it is self-declared or verified at sale, whether destination and end-user screening happens, and who must sign. This is what distinguishes 'formally restricted, sold to anyone with a credit card' from 'genuinely screened'.

sources.description: source ids; each must exist in data/sources/
